thread:
maria: handing off the night shift to @jason. Quick summary of current state: brief spike of 504s on /v1/generate starting ~23:20 UTC, error rate ~3x baseline but trending down after rolling back a canary. Impact: small subset of tenant traffic (5%) — some retries visible in logs. Primary = jason, secondary = alex. I'll be reachable until 00:15 UTC for any context. :wave:

jason: ack. I can take primary through 08:00 UTC local. what's the paging rule here? when do I escalate to sre-manager? :eyes:

maria: page for Sev1 (customer-facing outage / sustained API errors >10m) immediately. For elevated but partial impact (like this), treat as Sev2: watch for sustained increase >30m or error rate >5x background, then escalate. If you get a pager and can't respond in 5m -> escalate to sre-manager. If you need help with mitigation (rollbacks, scaling), call them immediately. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: [ALERT] Pager triggered: API-504-high at 1845127000 — routed to oncall (jason) and oncall-rotation. Details: 325 events / 10m. Link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/ID-7021

alex: noted, I'll be secondary and on standby for DB or routing changes. if it looks like a config flake we'll coordinate on the bridge.

jason: thanks. can you paste the quick runbook pointer for escalations and the short commands?

maria: paste below — follow step 1-3 first, then escalate. also watch the healthcheck canary in console (route: /healthz/canary).

```
Escalation Matrix (short):
- Sev1 (total outage / P0): page oncall (primary) -> 5m no-ack -> page sre-manager -> 10m no-ack -> page exec-ops + dial-out.
- Sev2 (partial customer-impact / P1): page oncall -> if error rate grows >2x for 30m -> elevate to sre-manager.
- Performance-only (latency spikes): file ticket, set live dashboard, page only if SLOs breached for 1h.
Commands:
- Add capacity: `kubectl scale deployment inference --replicas=XX -n prod`
- Rollback canary: `replay --model-version stable --route canary`
- Dump recent 504s: `jq '.errors[] | select(.code==504)' logs/last_15m.json`
Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall/escalation-and-paging
```

jason: great, also what's the expected behavior for customer alerts? i.e., when do we send a status page or CS ping?

maria: customer notification: if we hit sustained 504s affecting >10% of traffic or any SEV1 that hits paying customers' SLAs -> trigger status page + notify CS within 15m. For partial impact, coordinate with CS via the '#cs-notify' template and include mitigations and ETA.

incident-bot: [INFO] Bridge created: https://meet.redwood/bridge/1845127890 — oncall invited.

jason: starting 15m watch on canary and error rate. will attempt to bump capacity by 1 node if we see recurrence. i'll post updates every 10 minutes or on any change.

alex: i'll standby. if you need me to perform the rollback i'll be ready — ping me directly.

maria: one more note on coverage gap: we have scheduled infra maintenance 02:00-03:00 UTC tomorrow which may reduce spare capacity in us-east. if you see queueing or backpressure then escalate earlier. I've added that to the header of the runbook.

jason: copy. I will also add a brief handoff note to the shift doc at the 07:45 check-in.

maria: thanks — oncall checklist for you: 1) monitor `api/504_rate` dashboard 2) have rollback command ready 3) keep bridge open for 30m after any mitigation. filing action items now. :white_check_mark:

sre-manager: pinging in — if you need me to join the bridge escalate ASAP. prefer to be paged after 2 failed mitigation attempts or 10m of no-ack on sev1. otherwise i'll monitor channel.

jason: will do. starting watch now. will ping if any changes.

maria: handing off complete. thanks all — closing thread for handoff but keep updating here for incident updates. :slightly_smiling_face:
